newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses led up by record Dow, stable dlr.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses led up by record Dow, stable dlr.

text.p: European bourses opened higher on Friday, led by a second consecutive record close by U.S. blue chips after a solid U.S. 30-year bond auction and a stabilisation of the dollar after Thursday's sharp fall.
"The environment has cleared up, the 30-year T-bond has risen and the dollar, whose weakness weighed on the market on Thursday morning, is doing better," a French dealer said.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 28 points in New York to close at 6,206 to post its first close above 6,200 on Thursday. The Dow was bolstered by good demand at the U.S. Treasury's bond sale that helped push long-term interest rates down in the United States and Europe, a strong earnings prediction from Intel Corp.
And the dollar recovered from its lows after the U.S. bond auction and a Japanese Economic Planning Agency minister said Japanese rates must be kept low for now.

Germany's IBIS Dax index followed the Dow's gains and hit a record high in pre-bourse electronic trading and when bourse trading strated the Dax also reached a record. A jump in German government bond prices, implying lower long-term interest rates, and a slight dollar recovery also helped the German index.
Swiss shares were seen in reach of a record high. Dealers speculated that if stocks could hold their positive bias, the SMI index could test its record high at 3,838.7 index points during the day.

In Paris, the blue-chip CAC-40 also got a lift, but dealers warned that gains could be limited before a three-day weekend. Some also said the index needed to take a breather after recent gains to levels not seen in about two years before resuming its climb higher again.

Dutch shares were also boosted by strong third-quarter earnings from Unilever. Unilever shares surged 12.50 guilders, or 4.85 percent, at the open after its third-quarter results reached the top of most analysts' expectations.
The most tentative gains were made in Britain, where inflation and interest rate fears kept markets on edge.

The Confederation of British Industry said in a report that October UK retail sales rose at the fastest rate somce 1988, which highlighted again the Bank of England's forecast on Wednesday that inflation and interest rates were set to rise.
"With inflation fears around, people are still scared this market will crack," said a senior equities dealer.
Further worries that could cap gains on London's blue-chip FTSE-100 stock index came from sterling's recent surge, prompting fears the strong currency will start to carve into corporate earnings.
By 1005 GMT, sterling was at $1.6525, up from $1.6481 in late European trading on Thursday.

In other currencies, the Australian dollar closed at a three-month low against the yen overnight. Ideas of higher Japanese interest rates coupled with the recent cut in official Australian rates sharply narrowed interest rate spreads between Japan and Australia and prompted Japanese investors to move money back to Japan.
"Capital flows from Japan and the perceptions thereof, are easily the dominant influence at the moment," said Tim Moloney, an economist at Commonwealth Bank in Australia.
At 1020 GMT, Australian dollar/yen was quoted at 88.12.
CURRENCIES AT 1020 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5095 marks and 111.85 yen, compared with 1.5073 marks and 111.38 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1020 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 13.3 points higher at 3,913.70.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 3.50 at 2,215.31
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index rose 28.29 at 2,741.51.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1030 GMT
Gold fixed at $378.35 compared with Thursday's close of $379.45.
